# Ashok Reddy Advices Online Water Quality Monitoring, Accurate Tanker Filling Records

Telangana

DC Correspondent

22 Oct 2026 1:10 PM IST22 Oct 2026 1:10 PM IST

## Ashok Reddy examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically

x

Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspecting Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday. (Photo: By Arrangement)

As Preferred  
Source

**Hyderabad:** Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspected Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday.

He examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically. He suggested setting up filling marks to accurately identify the quantity of water filled in tankers.

He ordered to mandatorily record the quantity of water filled in each tanker and filling details. Reddy asked for continuous monitoring of the quality of purified water and supply quantity and advised to promote the use of purified water for construction sector, road cleanliness, dust control, and gardens.

He asked officials to accord priority to use purified water to reduce pressure on drinking water resources.

( Source : Deccan Chronicle )

What is the recommended dosage of bleaching powder for 15,000 m3?

Titles are generated by AI from Meta

Calculation for quantity of Bleaching Powder :-

• Recommended dosage 10 to 15 ppm active chlorine (10 ppm for example)

• 1 ppm = 1 mg/litre of water or 1 gram per tonne of water (10 ppm means 10 g per tonne or m3)

• Example 1 ha pond with 1.5 m water (1 ha= 10,000m2)

• Total volume of water = 10,000 x 1.5 = 15,000 m3

• Quantity of chlorine required = 10 x 15,000 = 150000 g or 150 Kg

• Bleaching powder contains 30-33% chlorine (say 30%), so 1 Kg of bleaching powder contains only 300 g chlorine (0.3 kg)

• So for achieving 150 Kg chlorine , divide 150/0.3 = 500 Kg bleaching powder.

Background
1) In partnership with the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), the Nobel Laureate Prof. Dr. Michael Kremer
and his team, "Evidence Action," have undertaken a structured pilot study to conduct a comprehensive
evaluation of in-line chlorination (ILC) technologies suitable for implementation in both Single Village
Scheme (SVS) and Multi Village Scheme (MVS). The pilot study was carried out in three States i.e.,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
2) The pilot study assessed three categories of devices within the SVS, encompassing
o tablet-based passive in-line chlorination devices (Easol PureALL 100 - recommended by the Standing
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation);
o non-electric liquid chlorine dosing devices (HiSafe Chloritron – recommended by the Technical
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation); and
o electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps (from the market).
3) To disseminate the outcome of the pilot study, a “National Symposium of Safe Water and Disinfection/
Chlorination Initiatives” was held on 02.02.2024 at SPM-NIWAS, Kolkata.
4) All the States/ UTs and Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur & IIT Guwahati were asked to submit a
presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives implementedby them.
5) The Symposium was attended by officials from various States/ UTs, Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur &
IIT Guwahati, academic institutions, private sector players, research organizations, and WASH community
organizations.

• We’ve developed a complementary technology, In-Line Chlorination (ILC) that is 
installed directly into a waterpoint’s pipes, automatically chlorinating all

• ILC enables us to reach new peri-urban and urban communities, which is

programs that do it

Before initiating the pilot, we conducted a 
comprehensive technology landscape analysis and 
infrastructure survey to understand the opportunity
Infrastructure survey
• Surveyed 151 water points across 9 Indian states
• Identified three promising intervention points:
– Single Village Schemes (SVS) tanks – groundwater based systems that service only a 
single village and are infrequently treated
– Multi-Village Schemes (MVS) intermediaries – MVS service more than one village and are 
often treated centrally. Schemes can run hundreds of miles and may require ‘topping up’
– MVS tanks – MVS often have a village-level tank with similar infrastructure to SVS tanks
Technology landscape analysis
• Rigorous process, including reviewing JJM approved technologies, hiring a local 
water technical consultant, and interviewing partners and academics
• Ultimately recommended chlorine due to its strong evidence base and ability to 
procure suitable devices that are “Made in India” Page no: 14

Since March 2023, we’ve been piloting three different 
water chlorination technologies across Madhya Pradesh
• We installed devices in 7 sites across the state 
across 3 different districts
• We tested three different technologies as part of 
the pilot to ensure we’d find a scalable solution
- Tablet-based dosers are a simple, low 
maintenance technology
- Electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps support 
large systems and have a robust existing supply 
chain
- Non-electric liquid chlorine dumps are a blend 
between the other two technologies

Chlorine is one of the most widely used and 
effective solutions to delivering safe water
Evidence suggests that chlorine reduces 
the odds of all-cause U5 mortality by 
about 25%
• Unsafe water is a leading cause of 
diarrhea, which causes millions of 
deaths worldwide, especially in 
children under 5
• Chlorination helps kill the 
bacterial agents that cause diarrhea
Chlorination is widely used globally and 
is endorsed by the World Health 
Organization
• Nobel Laureate Michael Kremer and co-
authors analyzed multiple RCTs to 
conclude that safe water treatment 
reduces the odds of all-cause U5 
mortality by about 25%
• Chlorine is officially endorsed by the 
World Health Organization and is included 
in the Guidelines for Drinking Water 
Quality (GDWQ)
• Water treatment via chlorination is widely 
used in treatment plants across the globe
• Evidence from Nobel Laureate Michael 
Kremer* and colleagues suggest that 
chlorination is more than 45 times as cost-
effective as the WHO’s threshold for 
“highly cost -effective interventions”
*Source: Water Treatment and Child Mortality: A Meta-analysis and Cost-
effectiveness Analysis

About Tablet based dosers
• Tablet-based dosers are simple In-Line 
Chlorination (ILC) devices, capable of 
treating 2,00,000 liters of water daily
• EAII recommends a design heavily based on 
the open-source CTI-8
• The technology has no mechanical moving 
parts and doesn’t require electricity
• The devices store chlorine tablets inside 
the device and are installed at the 
bypass line of waterpoints
Page no: 31

Tablet-based dosers can be easily and 
quickly constructed using commonly available 
parts 
• Construction requires only cheap 
and widely available parts like 
PVC, UPVC, and Acrylic
• Devices can be built within 4-6 
hours  
• Assembly can be led by a 
relatively low skilled plumber or 
fitter
• Necessary tools simple, such as 
cutting tools and PVC glue 
Page no: 32

Some considerations for installation of tablet 
based dosers
• Device enclosures are metal mesh cages with 
an opaque roof that enclose the entire 
device
• The enclosure will be securely fixed to the 
ground
• The roofing is constructed to protect the 
devices from the weather, including direct 
sunlight and rain
• The devices will have a lockable gate to 
ensure secure and easy maintenance

# Ashok Reddy Advices Online Water Quality Monitoring, Accurate Tanker Filling Records

Telangana

DC Correspondent

22 Oct 2026 1:10 PM IST22 Oct 2026 1:10 PM IST

## Ashok Reddy examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically

x

Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspecting Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday. (Photo: By Arrangement)

As Preferred  
Source

**Hyderabad:** Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspected Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday.

He examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically. He suggested setting up filling marks to accurately identify the quantity of water filled in tankers.

He ordered to mandatorily record the quantity of water filled in each tanker and filling details. Reddy asked for continuous monitoring of the quality of purified water and supply quantity and advised to promote the use of purified water for construction sector, road cleanliness, dust control, and gardens.

He asked officials to accord priority to use purified water to reduce pressure on drinking water resources.

( Source : Deccan Chronicle )

records.visible_text:
What is the recommended dosage of bleaching powder for 15,000 m3?

Titles are generated by AI from Meta

Calculation for quantity of Bleaching Powder :-

• Recommended dosage 10 to 15 ppm active chlorine (10 ppm for example)

• 1 ppm = 1 mg/litre of water or 1 gram per tonne of water (10 ppm means 10 g per tonne or m3)

• Example 1 ha pond with 1.5 m water (1 ha= 10,000m2)

• Total volume of water = 10,000 x 1.5 = 15,000 m3

• Quantity of chlorine required = 10 x 15,000 = 150000 g or 150 Kg

• Bleaching powder contains 30-33% chlorine (say 30%), so 1 Kg of bleaching powder contains only 300 g chlorine (0.3 kg)

• So for achieving 150 Kg chlorine , divide 150/0.3 = 500 Kg bleaching powder.

Titles are generated by AI from Meta

Calculation for quantity of Bleaching Powder :-

• Recommended dosage 10 to 15 ppm active chlorine (10 ppm for example)

• 1 ppm = 1 mg/litre of water or 1 gram per tonne of water (10 ppm means 10 g per tonne or m3)

• Example 1 ha pond with 1.5 m water (1 ha= 10,000m2)

• Total volume of water = 10,000 x 1.5 = 15,000 m3

• Quantity of chlorine required = 10 x 15,000 = 150000 g or 150 Kg

• Bleaching powder contains 30-33% chlorine (say 30%), so 1 Kg of bleaching powder contains only 300 g chlorine (0.3 kg)

• So for achieving 150 Kg chlorine , divide 150/0.3 = 500 Kg bleaching powder.

Contents
1) Background 
2) India Safe Water Program & ILC Implementation by Evidence Action
3) Presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives by the Professor Chair

o Andhra Pradesh

Contents
o Mizoram

o Rajasthan
o Sikkim 
o Tamil Nadu
o Telangana
o Tripura
o Uttar Pradesh
o West Bengal
Page no: 3

Background
1) In partnership with the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), the Nobel Laureate Prof. Dr. Michael Kremer
and his team, "Evidence Action," have undertaken a structured pilot study to conduct a comprehensive
evaluation of in-line chlorination (ILC) technologies suitable for implementation in both Single Village
Scheme (SVS) and Multi Village Scheme (MVS). The pilot study was carried out in three States i.e.,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
2) The pilot study assessed three categories of devices within the SVS, encompassing
o tablet-based passive in-line chlorination devices (Easol PureALL 100 - recommended by the Standing
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation);
o non-electric liquid chlorine dosing devices (HiSafe Chloritron – recommended by the Technical
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation); and
o electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps (from the market).
3) To disseminate the outcome of the pilot study, a “National Symposium of Safe Water and Disinfection/
Chlorination Initiatives” was held on 02.02.2024 at SPM-NIWAS, Kolkata.
4) All the States/ UTs and Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur & IIT Guwahati were asked to submit a
presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives implementedby them.
5) The Symposium was attended by officials from various States/ UTs, Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur &
IIT Guwahati, academic institutions, private sector players, research organizations, and WASH community
organizations.

Background
1) In partnership with the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), the Nobel Laureate Prof. Dr. Michael Kremer
and his team, "Evidence Action," have undertaken a structured pilot study to conduct a comprehensive
evaluation of in-line chlorination (ILC) technologies suitable for implementation in both Single Village
Scheme (SVS) and Multi Village Scheme (MVS). The pilot study was carried out in three States i.e.,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
2) The pilot study assessed three categories of devices within the SVS, encompassing
o tablet-based passive in-line chlorination devices (Easol PureALL 100 - recommended by the Standing
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation);
o non-electric liquid chlorine dosing devices (HiSafe Chloritron – recommended by the Technical
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation); and
o electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps (from the market).
3) To disseminate the outcome of the pilot study, a “National Symposium of Safe Water and Disinfection/
Chlorination Initiatives” was held on 02.02.2024 at SPM-NIWAS, Kolkata.
4) All the States/ UTs and Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur & IIT Guwahati were asked to submit a
presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives implementedby them.
5) The Symposium was attended by officials from various States/ UTs, Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur &
IIT Guwahati, academic institutions, private sector players, research organizations, and WASH community
organizations.

records.visible_text:
What is the recommended dosage of bleaching powder for 15,000 m3?

Titles are generated by AI from Meta

Calculation for quantity of Bleaching Powder :-

• Recommended dosage 10 to 15 ppm active chlorine (10 ppm for example)

• 1 ppm = 1 mg/litre of water or 1 gram per tonne of water (10 ppm means 10 g per tonne or m3)

• Example 1 ha pond with 1.5 m water (1 ha= 10,000m2)

• Total volume of water = 10,000 x 1.5 = 15,000 m3

• Quantity of chlorine required = 10 x 15,000 = 150000 g or 150 Kg

• Bleaching powder contains 30-33% chlorine (say 30%), so 1 Kg of bleaching powder contains only 300 g chlorine (0.3 kg)

• So for achieving 150 Kg chlorine , divide 150/0.3 = 500 Kg bleaching powder.

# Ashok Reddy Advices Online Water Quality Monitoring, Accurate Tanker Filling Records

Telangana

DC Correspondent

22 Oct 2026 1:10 PM IST22 Oct 2026 1:10 PM IST

## Ashok Reddy examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically

x

Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspecting Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday. (Photo: By Arrangement)

As Preferred  
Source

**Hyderabad:** Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspected Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday.

He examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically. He suggested setting up filling marks to accurately identify the quantity of water filled in tankers.

He ordered to mandatorily record the quantity of water filled in each tanker and filling details. Reddy asked for continuous monitoring of the quality of purified water and supply quantity and advised to promote the use of purified water for construction sector, road cleanliness, dust control, and gardens.

He asked officials to accord priority to use purified water to reduce pressure on drinking water resources.

( Source : Deccan Chronicle )

India Southern States Telangana Hyderabad

What is the recommended dosage of bleaching powder for 15,000 m3?

Titles are generated by AI from Meta

Calculation for quantity of Bleaching Powder :-

• Recommended dosage 10 to 15 ppm active chlorine (10 ppm for example)

• 1 ppm = 1 mg/litre of water or 1 gram per tonne of water (10 ppm means 10 g per tonne or m3)

• Example 1 ha pond with 1.5 m water (1 ha= 10,000m2)

• Total volume of water = 10,000 x 1.5 = 15,000 m3

• Quantity of chlorine required = 10 x 15,000 = 150000 g or 150 Kg

• Bleaching powder contains 30-33% chlorine (say 30%), so 1 Kg of bleaching powder contains only 300 g chlorine (0.3 kg)

• So for achieving 150 Kg chlorine , divide 150/0.3 = 500 Kg bleaching powder.

Background
1) In partnership with the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), the Nobel Laureate Prof. Dr. Michael Kremer
and his team, "Evidence Action," have undertaken a structured pilot study to conduct a comprehensive
evaluation of in-line chlorination (ILC) technologies suitable for implementation in both Single Village
Scheme (SVS) and Multi Village Scheme (MVS). The pilot study was carried out in three States i.e.,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
2) The pilot study assessed three categories of devices within the SVS, encompassing
o tablet-based passive in-line chlorination devices (Easol PureALL 100 - recommended by the Standing
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation);
o non-electric liquid chlorine dosing devices (HiSafe Chloritron – recommended by the Technical
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation); and
o electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps (from the market).
3) To disseminate the outcome of the pilot study, a “National Symposium of Safe Water and Disinfection/
Chlorination Initiatives” was held on 02.02.2024 at SPM-NIWAS, Kolkata.
4) All the States/ UTs and Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur & IIT Guwahati were asked to submit a
presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives implementedby them.
5) The Symposium was attended by officials from various States/ UTs, Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur &
IIT Guwahati, academic institutions, private sector players, research organizations, and WASH community
organizations.

**Hyderabad:** Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspected Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday.

He examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically. He suggested setting up filling marks to accurately identify the quantity of water filled in tankers.

He ordered to mandatorily record the quantity of water filled in each tanker and filling details. Reddy asked for continuous monitoring of the quality of purified water and supply quantity and advised to promote the use of purified water for construction sector, road cleanliness, dust control, and gardens.

He asked officials to accord priority to use purified water to reduce pressure on drinking water resources.

Background
1) In partnership with the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), the Nobel Laureate Prof. Dr. Michael Kremer
and his team, "Evidence Action," have undertaken a structured pilot study to conduct a comprehensive
evaluation of in-line chlorination (ILC) technologies suitable for implementation in both Single Village
Scheme (SVS) and Multi Village Scheme (MVS). The pilot study was carried out in three States i.e.,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
2) The pilot study assessed three categories of devices within the SVS, encompassing
o tablet-based passive in-line chlorination devices (Easol PureALL 100 - recommended by the Standing
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation);
o non-electric liquid chlorine dosing devices (HiSafe Chloritron – recommended by the Technical
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation); and
o electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps (from the market).
3) To disseminate the outcome of the pilot study, a “National Symposium of Safe Water and Disinfection/
Chlorination Initiatives” was held on 02.02.2024 at SPM-NIWAS, Kolkata.
4) All the States/ UTs and Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur & IIT Guwahati were asked to submit a
presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives implementedby them.
5) The Symposium was attended by officials from various States/ UTs, Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur &
IIT Guwahati, academic institutions, private sector players, research organizations, and WASH community
organizations.

## Ashok Reddy examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically

As Preferred

**Hyderabad:** Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspected Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday.

He examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically. He suggested setting up filling marks to accurately identify the quantity of water filled in tankers.

He ordered to mandatorily record the quantity of water filled in each tanker and filling details. Reddy asked for continuous monitoring of the quality of purified water and supply quantity and advised to promote the use of purified water for construction sector, road cleanliness, dust control, and gardens.

He asked officials to accord priority to use purified water to reduce pressure on drinking water resources.

Background
1) In partnership with the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), the Nobel Laureate Prof. Dr. Michael Kremer
and his team, "Evidence Action," have undertaken a structured pilot study to conduct a comprehensive
evaluation of in-line chlorination (ILC) technologies suitable for implementation in both Single Village
Scheme (SVS) and Multi Village Scheme (MVS). The pilot study was carried out in three States i.e.,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
2) The pilot study assessed three categories of devices within the SVS, encompassing
o tablet-based passive in-line chlorination devices (Easol PureALL 100 - recommended by the Standing
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation);
o non-electric liquid chlorine dosing devices (HiSafe Chloritron – recommended by the Technical
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation); and
o electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps (from the market).
3) To disseminate the outcome of the pilot study, a “National Symposium of Safe Water and Disinfection/
Chlorination Initiatives” was held on 02.02.2024 at SPM-NIWAS, Kolkata.
4) All the States/ UTs and Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur & IIT Guwahati were asked to submit a
presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives implementedby them.
5) The Symposium was attended by officials from various States/ UTs, Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur &
IIT Guwahati, academic institutions, private sector players, research organizations, and WASH community
organizations.

date_mentions.literal_context:
Background
1) In partnership with the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), the Nobel Laureate Prof. Dr. Michael Kremer
and his team, "Evidence Action," have undertaken a structured pilot study to conduct a comprehensive
evaluation of in-line chlorination (ILC) technologies suitable for implementation in both Single Village
Scheme (SVS) and Multi Village Scheme (MVS). The pilot study was carried out in three States i.e.,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
2) The pilot study assessed three categories of devices within the SVS, encompassing
o tablet-based passive in-line chlorination devices (Easol PureALL 100 - recommended by the Standing
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation);
o non-electric liquid chlorine dosing devices (HiSafe Chloritron – recommended by the Technical
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation); and
o electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps (from the market).
3) To disseminate the outcome of the pilot study, a “National Symposium of Safe Water and Disinfection/
Chlorination Initiatives” was held on 02.02.2024 at SPM-NIWAS, Kolkata.
4) All the States/ UTs and Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur & IIT Guwahati were asked to submit a
presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives implementedby them.
5) The Symposium was attended by officials from various States/ UTs, Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur &
IIT Guwahati, academic institutions, private sector players, research organizations, and WASH community
organizations.

records.visible_text:
What is the recommended dosage of bleaching powder for 15,000 m3?

Titles are generated by AI from Meta

Calculation for quantity of Bleaching Powder :-

• Recommended dosage 10 to 15 ppm active chlorine (10 ppm for example)

• 1 ppm = 1 mg/litre of water or 1 gram per tonne of water (10 ppm means 10 g per tonne or m3)

• Example 1 ha pond with 1.5 m water (1 ha= 10,000m2)

• Total volume of water = 10,000 x 1.5 = 15,000 m3

• Quantity of chlorine required = 10 x 15,000 = 150000 g or 150 Kg

• Bleaching powder contains 30-33% chlorine (say 30%), so 1 Kg of bleaching powder contains only 300 g chlorine (0.3 kg)

• So for achieving 150 Kg chlorine , divide 150/0.3 = 500 Kg bleaching powder.

Background
1) In partnership with the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), the Nobel Laureate Prof. Dr. Michael Kremer
and his team, "Evidence Action," have undertaken a structured pilot study to conduct a comprehensive
evaluation of in-line chlorination (ILC) technologies suitable for implementation in both Single Village
Scheme (SVS) and Multi Village Scheme (MVS). The pilot study was carried out in three States i.e.,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
2) The pilot study assessed three categories of devices within the SVS, encompassing
o tablet-based passive in-line chlorination devices (Easol PureALL 100 - recommended by the Standing
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation);
o non-electric liquid chlorine dosing devices (HiSafe Chloritron – recommended by the Technical
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation); and
o electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps (from the market).
3) To disseminate the outcome of the pilot study, a “National Symposium of Safe Water and Disinfection/
Chlorination Initiatives” was held on 02.02.2024 at SPM-NIWAS, Kolkata.
4) All the States/ UTs and Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur & IIT Guwahati were asked to submit a
presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives implementedby them.
5) The Symposium was attended by officials from various States/ UTs, Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur &
IIT Guwahati, academic institutions, private sector players, research organizations, and WASH community
organizations.

# Ashok Reddy Advices Online Water Quality Monitoring, Accurate Tanker Filling Records

Telangana

DC Correspondent

22 Oct 2026 1:10 PM IST22 Oct 2026 1:10 PM IST

## Ashok Reddy examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically

x

Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspecting Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday. (Photo: By Arrangement)

As Preferred  
Source

**Hyderabad:** Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspected Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday.

He examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically. He suggested setting up filling marks to accurately identify the quantity of water filled in tankers.

He ordered to mandatorily record the quantity of water filled in each tanker and filling details. Reddy asked for continuous monitoring of the quality of purified water and supply quantity and advised to promote the use of purified water for construction sector, road cleanliness, dust control, and gardens.

He asked officials to accord priority to use purified water to reduce pressure on drinking water resources.

( Source : Deccan Chronicle )

S10.literal_context:
Background
1) In partnership with the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), the Nobel Laureate Prof. Dr. Michael Kremer
and his team, "Evidence Action," have undertaken a structured pilot study to conduct a comprehensive
evaluation of in-line chlorination (ILC) technologies suitable for implementation in both Single Village
Scheme (SVS) and Multi Village Scheme (MVS). The pilot study was carried out in three States i.e.,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
2) The pilot study assessed three categories of devices within the SVS, encompassing
o tablet-based passive in-line chlorination devices (Easol PureALL 100 - recommended by the Standing
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation);
o non-electric liquid chlorine dosing devices (HiSafe Chloritron – recommended by the Technical
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation); and
o electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps (from the market).
3) To disseminate the outcome of the pilot study, a “National Symposium of Safe Water and Disinfection/
Chlorination Initiatives” was held on 02.02.2024 at SPM-NIWAS, Kolkata.
4) All the States/ UTs and Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur & IIT Guwahati were asked to submit a
presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives implementedby them.
5) The Symposium was attended by officials from various States/ UTs, Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur &
IIT Guwahati, academic institutions, private sector players, research organizations, and WASH community
organizations.

What is the recommended dosage of bleaching powder for 15,000 m3?

Titles are generated by AI from Meta

Calculation for quantity of Bleaching Powder :-

• Recommended dosage 10 to 15 ppm active chlorine (10 ppm for example)

• 1 ppm = 1 mg/litre of water or 1 gram per tonne of water (10 ppm means 10 g per tonne or m3)

• Example 1 ha pond with 1.5 m water (1 ha= 10,000m2)

• Total volume of water = 10,000 x 1.5 = 15,000 m3

• Quantity of chlorine required = 10 x 15,000 = 150000 g or 150 Kg

• Bleaching powder contains 30-33% chlorine (say 30%), so 1 Kg of bleaching powder contains only 300 g chlorine (0.3 kg)

• So for achieving 150 Kg chlorine , divide 150/0.3 = 500 Kg bleaching powder.

Background
1) In partnership with the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), the Nobel Laureate Prof. Dr. Michael Kremer
and his team, "Evidence Action," have undertaken a structured pilot study to conduct a comprehensive
evaluation of in-line chlorination (ILC) technologies suitable for implementation in both Single Village
Scheme (SVS) and Multi Village Scheme (MVS). The pilot study was carried out in three States i.e.,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
2) The pilot study assessed three categories of devices within the SVS, encompassing
o tablet-based passive in-line chlorination devices (Easol PureALL 100 - recommended by the Standing
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation);
o non-electric liquid chlorine dosing devices (HiSafe Chloritron – recommended by the Technical
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation); and
o electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps (from the market).
3) To disseminate the outcome of the pilot study, a “National Symposium of Safe Water and Disinfection/
Chlorination Initiatives” was held on 02.02.2024 at SPM-NIWAS, Kolkata.
4) All the States/ UTs and Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur & IIT Guwahati were asked to submit a
presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives implementedby them.
5) The Symposium was attended by officials from various States/ UTs, Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur &
IIT Guwahati, academic institutions, private sector players, research organizations, and WASH community
organizations.

**Hyderabad:** Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspected Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday.

He examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically. He suggested setting up filling marks to accurately identify the quantity of water filled in tankers.

He ordered to mandatorily record the quantity of water filled in each tanker and filling details. Reddy asked for continuous monitoring of the quality of purified water and supply quantity and advised to promote the use of purified water for construction sector, road cleanliness, dust control, and gardens.

He asked officials to accord priority to use purified water to reduce pressure on drinking water resources.

Background
1) In partnership with the National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), the Nobel Laureate Prof. Dr. Michael Kremer
and his team, "Evidence Action," have undertaken a structured pilot study to conduct a comprehensive
evaluation of in-line chlorination (ILC) technologies suitable for implementation in both Single Village
Scheme (SVS) and Multi Village Scheme (MVS). The pilot study was carried out in three States i.e.,
Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan.
2) The pilot study assessed three categories of devices within the SVS, encompassing
o tablet-based passive in-line chlorination devices (Easol PureALL 100 - recommended by the Standing
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation);
o non-electric liquid chlorine dosing devices (HiSafe Chloritron – recommended by the Technical
Committee of the Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation); and
o electric liquid chlorine dosing pumps (from the market).
3) To disseminate the outcome of the pilot study, a “National Symposium of Safe Water and Disinfection/
Chlorination Initiatives” was held on 02.02.2024 at SPM-NIWAS, Kolkata.
4) All the States/ UTs and Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur & IIT Guwahati were asked to submit a
presentation on Safe Water and Disinfection/ Chlorination Initiatives implementedby them.
5) The Symposium was attended by officials from various States/ UTs, Professor Chair from IIT Kanpur &
IIT Guwahati, academic institutions, private sector players, research organizations, and WASH community
organizations.

**Hyderabad:** Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspected Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday.

He examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically. He suggested setting up filling marks to accurately identify the quantity of water filled in tankers.

He ordered to mandatorily record the quantity of water filled in each tanker and filling details. Reddy asked for continuous monitoring of the quality of purified water and supply quantity and advised to promote the use of purified water for construction sector, road cleanliness, dust control, and gardens.

# Ashok Reddy Advices Online Water Quality Monitoring, Accurate Tanker Filling Records

Telangana

DC Correspondent

22 Oct 2026 1:10 PM IST22 Oct 2026 1:10 PM IST

## Ashok Reddy examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically

x

Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspecting Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday. (Photo: By Arrangement)

As Preferred  
Source

**Hyderabad:** Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy inspected Kokapet Green Water Filling Station here on Thursday.

He examined purified water quality standards and test results at the filling station and instructed officials to register water quality test results online periodically. He suggested setting up filling marks to accurately identify the quantity of water filled in tankers.

He ordered to mandatorily record the quantity of water filled in each tanker and filling details. Reddy asked for continuous monitoring of the quality of purified water and supply quantity and advised to promote the use of purified water for construction sector, road cleanliness, dust control, and gardens.

He asked officials to accord priority to use purified water to reduce pressure on drinking water resources.

( Source : Deccan Chronicle )

India Southern States Telangana Hyderabad
